page: Google Cloud Platform c3d-highcpu-90 is a compute-focused virtual machine instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9B14 processor on the x86_64 architecture. The configuration supplies 90 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 45 physical cores via simultaneous multithreading, supported by 177.0 GB of system memory, which yields an approximate 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 1.97 GB per thread. The underlying hardware incorporates 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, along with advanced instruction sets including AVX-512, AVX512-VNNI, AVX512-BF16, and hardware-accelerated cryptographic extensions like VAES and SHA-NI.

The instance does not include integrated local NVMe storage or dedicated GPU acceleration, requiring persistent disk options across the network for data retention. Benchmark metrics place the server in the top tier for multi-core computation and vector-intensive calculations. It scores 87,356.8 on PassMark CPU, 113,336.73 on extended CPU instruction tests, and achieves top decile results in Clang compilation and ray tracing. Memory throughput scales up to 215.31 GB/sec on uncached large reads, while multi-core stress testing yields 129,122.14 iterations in stress-ng.

Cost efficiency is balanced toward organizations needing dense compute parallelism without paying for excessive memory footprints or dedicated accelerator hardware. Workload execution shines in CI/CD pipeline compilation, CPU-based machine learning inference, static web serving (benchmarked at 51.24 GB/sec), and distributed batch processing routines.
